subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw core add `gateway.peers` and cross-gateway session-tool routing now, and if so what URL, credential, identity, and scope boundary must the feature obey?
rationale: This is not just a helper change: it adds a new remote control path for session messages and spawns, touches config, and can move operator-authenticated traffic across gateway trust boundaries.

options.title: Design the core contract first
options.body: Define the peer identity, credential, URL allowlist, replay/idempotency, and session-visibility contract before merging code in core.

options.title: Narrow this PR to configured peers only
options.body: Keep raw `gatewayUrl` on the existing allowlisted path, require explicit peer credentials or a documented no-auth mode, and prove both send and spawn against two real gateways.

options.title: Pause for the federation FRD
options.body: Close or hold this PR until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 settles the broader gateway-to-gateway protocol and trust model.

recommendation.title: Design the core contract first
recommendation.body: Define the peer identity, credential, URL allowlist, replay/idempotency, and session-visibility contract before merging code in core.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history for gateway protocol/auth and session-tool architecture points to this owner candidate.
